title: Mexico’s Formal Employment Reaches Historic High of 23.08 Million Jobs
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [November 9, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/empleo-formal-alcanza-
maximo-historico-de-23-08-millones-de-puestos-imss/), a Mexican investigative
journalism magazine._

At the close of October 2026, Mexico reached a historic high of **23,088,353
jobs registered with the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS)** , of which
20,043,824 are permanent, the highest figure for any month since records
began, the agency reported.

In its affiliation report for October 31, the IMSS detailed that 161,077 jobs
were created during that month, a monthly growth of 0.7 percent. With this,
formal job creation accumulated so far this year reached 571,277 positions.

Of the total jobs registered, 86.8 percent are permanent positions and 13.2
percent are temporary. In the last 12 months, affiliation grew by 299,180
jobs, equivalent to an annual change of 1.3 percent.

By economic sector, the largest annual increases were recorded in
transportation and communications, with 6.7 percent; extractive activities,
with 5.5 percent; and construction, with 3.4 percent. By state, Chiapas,
Oaxaca and Hidalgo stood out with growth above 4.5 percent.

The average base contribution wage of jobs registered with the IMSS reached
664.7 pesos per day in October, the highest level for that month and the sixth
highest recorded for any month. Compared with October 2025, the wage increased
by 42.7 nominal pesos, one of the largest increases for that month since
records began.

Regarding **employment on digital platforms, the IMSS counted 1,748,740 people
benefiting** from the reform that regulates this type of work. Of that total,
229,249 exceeded the monthly net income threshold and were registered as jobs
by 18 digital platforms, which allows them to access the institute's five
insurance programs.

During October, affiliation under this modality increased by 21,862 jobs. In
the last 12 months, growth was 79,126 jobs, equivalent to 52.7 percent. The
associated average daily wage stood at 420.3 pesos.

People who did not reach the monthly net income threshold keep occupational
risk insurance coverage, which includes medical care and economic benefits in
case of work-related accidents or illnesses, under the conditions set out in
the reform.

The report also recorded **58,931 jobs associated with domestic workers** ,
with an average daily wage of 518.7 pesos and 96,588 potential beneficiaries.

As for independent workers, the **IMSS counted 485,727 jobs** , with an
average daily wage of 369.3 pesos. This scheme allows access to the
institute's five insurance programs and extends coverage to legal
beneficiaries.

As of October 31, the IMSS had 1,008,887 employer registrations, a monthly
increase of 127 registrations, equivalent to 0.01 percent. However, the annual
comparison showed a decrease of 2.9 percent.

The agency clarified that employer registrations are administrative units used
to identify and track employers' obligations, so they are not directly
equivalent to the number of companies or businesses. Their reduction does not
necessarily imply closures, as it can also reflect data cleanup, validation
and updating processes.

In addition, at the close of October, 8,402,835 people were enrolled in
Optional Insurance (Seguro Facultativo); 138,467 in Family Health Insurance;
and 263,802 in the Voluntary Continuation of the Mandatory Regime scheme.
